description: List sorted relative names of regular files beneath a directory using the retained recursive filesystem iterator.

interface.semantic_input: Path resolving to a readable directory
interface.semantic_output: Ordered names of regular files relative to the supplied root. JSON transfer was tested on valid UTF-8 path strings.

resources: Collects all selected path strings and sorts them in memory. Directory traversal and memory limits are unknown.

preconditions.detail: The root must resolve to a traversable directory for successful enumeration.

postconditions.detail: Returned sorted relative names including hidden, nested and hard-linked entries. Child symlinks, a FIFO and directories were excluded. A directory symlink supplied as the root was traversed.

refinements.detail: Child symlink behavior and root resolution have distinct scope. A dangling root and a regular-file root each raised filesystem_error in the direct client.

effects.detail: Enumerates filesystem entries. In the ordinary JSON program the three failed input cases preserved a pre-existing destination and left an initially absent destination absent.

invariants.detail: Two trees created in different orders produced the same path sequence. A shallow traversal returned a different answer on nested files.

formal_predicates.detail: No universal traversal or error guarantee was proved. JSON round-trip of arbitrary POSIX pathname bytes is unqualified.

mathematical_properties.detail: No general sorting property was independently proved.

state_protocol.detail: There is one synchronous invocation and no caller-visible retained object.

ownership.detail: Borrows the root C string for the call and returns a vector of owned strings by value.

concurrency.detail: Concurrent directory changes, permission changes and stable snapshots have not been qualified.

upstream_usage.detail: The pinned project catalog declares recursive_files and an example with a top-level and a nested file.

specification_question.detail: The retained binding exposes only the root path.
